seoTitle: How to Enter Your IRS IP PIN in TurboTax
metaDescription: Find the Identity Protection PIN question under Other tax situations in TurboTax, answer Yes, and enter your IRS-issued IP PIN before you file.
intro: If the IRS has issued you an Identity Protection PIN, either because of a past identity theft case or because you opted into the program voluntarily, entering it correctly in TurboTax isn't optional — a missing or wrong IP PIN can get your e-filed return rejected outright. TurboTax doesn't put this field somewhere obvious like the main info screen; it's buried a few clicks into the federal section under a heading most filers skip past. This guide shows exactly where that question lives, what TurboTax asks before showing you the entry field, and where to go afterward if you need to double check it.

steps.heading: Sign in and open Tax home
steps.body: Sign in to TurboTax with your phone number, email, or user ID from the "Let's get you in to TurboTax" card, which sits next to the site's marketing content about expert-reviewed returns. Once you're in, you land on Tax home, greeted by name with a status checklist running down the left side — My info, Federal, State, Final review, and File — each marked with a green check once complete. The IP PIN question lives inside Federal, so head there next rather than looking for it on this landing screen.

image.caption: TurboTax's sign-in screen, the starting point before you can reach the Identity Protection PIN question inside your return.

steps.heading: Go into Federal from Tax home
steps.body: From Tax home, click into Federal in the left-hand checklist, which expands into sub-sections: Income, Deductions & credits, Other tax situations, and Federal review. The IP PIN field is not under Income or Deductions, which trips people up since a PIN feels like a personal-info item — it's actually filed under Other tax situations, TurboTax's catch-all for less common items like estimated tax penalties and identity-related forms.

image.caption: The Federal section expanded from Tax home, with Other tax situations as the sub-section that holds the Identity Protection PIN question.

steps.heading: Answer "Were you assigned an Identity Protection PIN?"
steps.body: Inside Other tax situations, under a group called Other Return Info, TurboTax asks directly: "Were you assigned an Identity Protection PIN?" with a short explanation that an IP PIN protects you from tax-related identity theft, and a note about two ways you'd have one — either the IRS mailed you a CP01A notice each January with a new PIN, or if you voluntarily joined the IP PIN program, you'd need to retrieve it online instead since no CP01A is mailed for opt-in participants. Click Yes if either applies to you, or No if you've never been issued one.

image.caption: TurboTax's "Were you assigned an Identity Protection PIN?" screen, explaining the CP01A notice and the online retrieval option for voluntary participants.

steps.heading: Enter the PIN exactly as issued
steps.body: Answering Yes opens a field for the six-digit IP PIN itself. Type it exactly as it appears on your CP01A notice or in your IRS online account — IP PINs reset every year, so a PIN from a prior tax season will not work and TurboTax should flag it as invalid if you try to reuse an old one. Double-check each digit before continuing, since a single wrong digit here is enough to trigger an e-file rejection later even though the rest of your return is correct.

steps.heading: Revisit the entry from the tax situations list if you need to check it
steps.body: Once entered, the Identity Protection PIN row appears in Your uncommon tax situations with an Edit button rather than Start, confirming the entry is saved — this is also where Identity Theft Affidavit and other less-common forms live if any of those apply to your situation too. If you need to update the PIN later, whether because you retrieved a corrected one from the IRS or made a typo, come back to this same screen and click Edit rather than searching for a different entry point.

image.caption: Your uncommon tax situations screen, showing Identity Protection PIN already entered with an Edit option, alongside the separate Identity Theft Affidavit.

steps.heading: Know what happens if you skip it
steps.body: If the IRS has you on record as needing an IP PIN and you file without one, expect an e-file rejection rather than a quiet acceptance — the IRS uses the PIN specifically to block returns filed under your Social Security number without it. If you've lost your PIN and can't find your CP01A notice, use the IRS's online Get an IP PIN tool to retrieve your current one rather than guessing or reusing an old number, since neither TurboTax nor the IRS can override this check for you.

faq.question: Where exactly is the IP PIN field in TurboTax?
faq.answer: Under Federal, then Other tax situations, then the Other Return Info group — TurboTax asks "Were you assigned an Identity Protection PIN?" and shows the entry field once you answer Yes.

faq.question: What happens if I don't enter my IP PIN?
faq.answer: A missing IP PIN when one is required typically causes your e-filed return to be rejected, since the IRS uses it specifically to verify returns filed under your Social Security number.

faq.question: Where do I get my IRS IP PIN if I've lost it?
faq.answer: Check your CP01A notice mailed each January if you're an assigned participant, or use the IRS's online Get an IP PIN tool if you voluntarily joined the program, since no notice is mailed for opt-in participants.

faq.question: Does everyone need an IP PIN to file in TurboTax?
faq.answer: No. Only taxpayers who have been issued one by the IRS — often due to a history of identity theft or by opting into the program — need to enter it; everyone else can answer No to the question.

faq.question: Can I reuse last year's IP PIN?
faq.answer: No. IP PINs reset every filing season, so entering a prior year's PIN will not work and should be flagged as invalid when you try to file.
